paragraphs: The 116i has been part of the 1 Series range since 2004, with the F20/F21 generation (2011–2019) using two distinct petrol engines under the same badge. Early cars (roughly 2011 to 2015) use the N13 — a 1.6-litre turbocharged four-cylinder. From 2015, BMW switched the 116i to the B38, a 1.5-litre three-cylinder unit that's part of BMW's newer modular engine family. The F70 generation launched in June 2024, but rebuild demand for this newest generation is still negligible. The 116i is no longer in production for the UK market, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 1.6-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine fitted to the 116i from 2011 to 2015 (F20/F21 generation). The N13 is BMW's first production turbocharged four-cylinder, and like many early turbo engines, timing chain guide wear is the most common issue we see. We replace the timing chain, guides, tensioners and gaskets as standard on every N13 rebuild.

The B38 is a 1.5-litre three-cylinder petrol engine, part of BMW's newer modular engine family introduced from 2015 onwards. It's a different unit from the N13 entirely — more modern, with improved timing chain design and generally better reliability. No widely-reported engine issue confirmed for this application. We service it to the same standard as our other 116i rebuilds.

compatibility.intro: Because the 116i spans two distinct engines across its F20/F21 production run, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N13 part will work on a B38 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N13 or B38) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 116i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
